descriptionChirho: The proper noun Megiddo (מְגִדּוֹ/מְגִדּוֹן), referring to the strategic Canaanite and later Israelite city located in the Jezreel Valley at a critical pass on the Via Maris trade route. It appears in conquest lists (Josh 12:21, 17:11; Judg 1:27, 5:19), Solomon's administrative districts (1 Kgs 4:12, 9:15), and as the site of King Josiah's death (2 Kgs 23:29-30; 2 Chr 35:22; Zech 12:11). All 12 occurrences refer to the same location: bare nominative and with conjunctive waw (Megiddo, 9x), with prepositions be-/min- 'in/from Megiddo' (2x), and the variant form Megiddon (1x). Multilingual evidence confirms a single referent: spa 'Meguido/en Meguido/de Meguido', hin 'मगिद्दो/मगिद्दोन', arb 'مَجِدّوَ/مَجِدُّونَ', kor '므깃도/므깃도에서', swa 'Megido/kutoka Megido'. The Megiddon variant (S109597) is an orthographic/dialectal alternation of the same toponym, not a distinct sense.
